scope: Red-team re-audit of the first full metric flower simulation claim
summary: The v1 300/300 force-closure claim is revoked because its six symmetric contacts were constructed rather than measured from the exact Sharpa pads, and its four stage artifacts lacked a common producer-bundle gate.
evidence: Measured active-frame Sharpa fingertip-anchor distances to the stem were 0.0815-0.1070 m, with zero frames containing two tips within 3 mm.
The original six-pad helper emitted six synthetic fingertip IDs even though the exact hand contract has five fingertips.

The corrected compiler rerun at outputs/foundation-contact/20260812T141600Z-recompile-superseded-full660-v1-lineage-v11 returns PARTIAL because the old artifacts lack bundle IDs, embedded source hashes, FPS lineage, and a hash-bound bundle manifest.
The new exact-contact path uses transformed Sharpa elastomer mesh vertices and no longer calls the six-pad fixture.
lessons: A force-closure evaluator must consume actual embodiment contact geometry; a mathematically passing fixture is not evidence that the rendered hand touched the object.
Individually valid stages cannot be combined unless source, frame indices, FPS, timeline, coordinate frame, instance IDs, producer ID, and hashes all agree.
limitations: The v1 video remains a visual simulation artifact but is not accepted physical grasp evidence.
The associated v1 VACE data requires re-export after a corrected full rollout.
next_actions: Complete an exact-pad full rollout and independent bundle compile before restoring any simulated force-closure claim.
